concerns.text: The plan proposes to generate **synthetic genre proportion vectors** (uniform Dirichlet) because the verified Last.fm dataset is unavailable. This substitution means the analysis will not use real musical‑preference data, so the core research question – whether personality traits correlate with actual listening behaviour – cannot be answered. It also violates FR‑001 (linked dataset) and undermines construct validity of the ‘genre preference’ measure.

The specification (FR‑003) requires **Pearson** correlation, yet the plan states it will compute **Spearman** correlations (and the research.md also selects Spearman). This methodological mismatch changes the statistical model and effect‑size interpretation, making the results non‑comparable to the spec’s expectations.

Effect‑size conversion is described as “Spearman ρ → rank‑biserial → Cohen’s d”. Converting a non‑parametric correlation to Cohen’s d is not standard and may produce misleading effect‑size estimates, especially when the underlying data are synthetic. This further weakens the validity of any claimed associations.
